hook: The queen who united Spain, conquered Granada and sent Columbus west.

pages.x: Isabella was born in 1451, daughter of the king of Castile, but with brothers ahead of her she was not expected to rule. Her half-brother, King Henry IV, tried to marry her to the much older king of Portugal. She refused.
In 1469 she secretly married Ferdinand, heir to Aragon, who rode to meet her disguised as a servant. They used a forged permission from the pope. The marriage joined Spain's two largest kingdoms.

When Henry died in 1474 she had herself proclaimed queen and won a five-year war against her rivals. She and Ferdinand ruled together as "the Catholic Monarchs", with a motto meaning that each was worth as much as the other.

After ten years of war they took Granada, the last Muslim kingdom in Spain, on 2 January 1492, ending almost 800 years of Muslim rule. The last sultan, it is said, wept as he looked back at the Alhambra.

The same year she ordered every Jew in her kingdoms to convert or leave; tens of thousands left. The Spanish Inquisition, which she and Ferdinand had set up in 1478, hunted those suspected of secretly keeping their old faith.
Also in 1492, after years of saying no, she agreed to pay for Christopher Columbus's voyage west across the Atlantic. His landing in the Americas began Spain's empire there.

Isabella united Spain with Ferdinand, finished the long reconquest of Spain and launched its empire in the Americas. She also set up the Inquisition and drove out the Jews. Her grandson Charles V ruled half the world.
pts: United Spain with Ferdinand of Aragon
Expelled the Jews and backed the Inquisition
